title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook: Onboarding, Escalation, Integration, Known Issues, Health Checks & QBRs
author: Ava Patel
body:
Overview:
This playbook consolidates Redwood's standard operating procedures for enterprise onboarding, escalation paths, integration best practices, known issues and workarounds, support process SLAs, routine health checks, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) preparation. Intended audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Support Engineers, Solutions Engineers, and Onboarding SREs.

Goals:
- Provide a single reference that reduces time-to-first-success for new enterprise customers.
- Ensure consistent, auditable escalation behavior for Sev1/Sev2 incidents.
- Capture integration checkpoints and common pitfalls to accelerate deployments.
- Define health check cadence, QBR artifacts, and owner responsibilities.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Dedicated and Private deployment customers, and hosted customers with enterprise contracts.
- Assumes customer has completed initial legal and security review and access has been provisioned to Redwood Console and required cloud endpoints.

Owner and RACI:
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Ava Patel)
- Technical owner: Onboarding SRE (Liam Chen)
- Escalation owner: Support Escalations (Miguel Torres)
- Reviewer group: Solutions Engineering, Platform, Security

Onboarding checklist (high-level):
1) Pre-kickoff (CSM):
   - Collect customer contacts: primary CSM, technical lead, security contact, legal billing.
   - Verify contract tier, SLA entitlements, and regions.
   - Provision tenant in Redwood Console; open onboarding ticket in Jira (project: CS-ONBOARD).
2) Kickoff (Week 0):
   - 60-minute kickoff covering architecture, security, integration plan, success metrics, and timeline.
   - Share onboarding runbook and access to shared Confluence space.
3) Integration (Weeks 1-3):
   - Network connectivity: validate VPC peering/VPN, CIDR allowlists, and inbound/outbound rules.
   - Auth: verify API keys, SSO/SAML setup, KMS/HSM integrations (if applicable).
   - Test vectors: run smoke tests for generation, embeddings, and stream responses.
4) Performance validation (Week 2-4):
   - Run baseline perf tests: 95th percentile latency target for sample workload.
   - Capture throughput targets and adjust batching, kv-cache and quantization profile recommendations.
5) Production cutover (Week 3-6):
   - Canary rollout: route 5-10% traffic for 24-72 hours, monitor metrics, and sign-off.
   - Post-cutover checklist and incident readiness review.

Integration guide (technical checklist):
- Network and Security:
  - Required egress endpoints: api.redwood-inference.internal, auth.redwood-inference.internal (provide specific IP ranges in customer ticket).
  - TLS: TLS1.2+ required; client certs optional for Private deployments.
  - Allowlist ports: 443 (API), 22 (optional for onprem support), ephemeral ports for data plane as documented.
- Authentication:
  - Recommended: short-lived API keys via Redwood Console or SSO with SCIM provisioning.
  - KMS integration: provide key ARNs and rotation schedule; verify encrypt-at-rest.
- Telemetry and Observability:
  - Provide examples: curl-based smoke test and structured log sample.
  - Recommend forwarding application logs to customer SIEM; expose per-route latency and token-cost metrics via Console.

Example smoke test (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b", "input":"Hello world", "max_tokens":32}'
```

Known issues and workarounds (summary):
- High initial latency for cold KV cache (Private/Dedicated):
  - Symptom: first requests after idle show 2-4x latency.
  - Workaround: enable warmup traffic (scheduled probes) or configure prefix caching for steady-state workloads.
- Tokenization mismatch with older SDK versions:
  - Symptom: generated text has unexpected splitting or off-by-one token counts.
  - Workaround: upgrade to SDK >= 1.4.2 or use server_side_tokenize flag in requests.
- Intermittent auth failures during key rotation:
  - Symptom: 401s for a short window during automated rotation.
  - Workaround: use overlapping key validity window and stagger rotation across client fleets.

Support and escalation process (procedural):
1) Triage (Support Tier 1):
   - Log incident in Zendesk with customer and product tags.
   - Perform initial diagnosis: reproduce, capture logs, collect request_id, model, route, timestamps.
   - If not resolved in 60 minutes for critical customer or 4 business hours otherwise, escalate to Tier 2.
2) Tier 2 (Support Engineers / Solutions Eng):
   - Deep-dive triage: review engine logs, pod-level metrics, KV cache state, batching queues, and model variant fallbacks.
   - Apply temporary mitigation (rate-limit, fallback model, restart worker pool) if needed.
   - Communicate status to customer every 30 minutes for Sev1, hourly for Sev2.
3) Escalation to SRE/Platform (Tier 3):
   - Criteria: suspected infra/GPU-fleet/networking/root-cause outside application surface or after 2 hours unresolved for Sev1.
   - SRE actions: run capacity checks, check autoscaler logs, validate kernel failures, escalate to on-call infra as needed.
4) Executive escalation / Customer Success leadership:
   - Triggered when customer executive requests or outage > 8 hours impacting production SLAs.

Escalation contact table (primary):
| Level | Role | Primary contact | Pager | Expected response time |
|------:|------|-----------------|-------|------------------------|
| Tier 1 | Support Engineer | support@redwood.ai | N/A | 15 min (ack) |
| Tier 2 | Solutions Engineer | se-oncall@redwood.ai | Pager: S2-team | 30 min |
| Tier 3 | Oncall SRE | oncall-sre@redwood.ai | Pager: SRE | 15 min |
| Exec | CS Lead | csm-leads@redwood.ai | Pager: Exec | 60 min |

Severity definitions and SLAs:
- Sev1 (Production outage): customer-facing outage preventing service usage. SLA: initial response in 15 min, update cadence 30 min, resolution target 4 hours for hosted; 8 hours for dedicated/private with agreed recovery plan.
- Sev2 (Degraded performance): significant impact but partial functionality. SLA: initial response 30 min, resolution target 24 hours.
- Sev3 (Minor): feature-level or non-critical. SLA: initial response 4 business hours, resolution target 7 days.

Health checks and monitoring cadence:
- Daily (CS/Support): check health dashboard for dedicated customers; look for token-cost spikes, 95th percentile latency, error rate (>1% threshold).
- Weekly (CS + Eng): review top 3 customer-facing errors, integration tickets open >7 days, and any regression alerts from Redwood Optimize.
- Monthly (CS + Product): review usage trends vs committed capacity, cost overruns >10%, and recommendations for batching/quantization.
- Quarterly (QBR): prepare artifacts (see QBR section).

QBR materials and template (owner: CSM):
- Required artifacts:
  - Executive summary (1 pager): adoption, uptime, cost per 1M tokens, major wins, and outstanding risks.
  - Technical appendix: latency/throughput graphs, top error types, security events, integration blockers.
  - Action items: roadmap alignment, optimization recommendations (batching/quantization), capacity adjustments.
- QBR cadence: customer-preferred frequency (standard = quarterly). CSM prepares draft two weeks before meeting and shares with Solutions Eng and SRE for technical review one week before.

Example QBR agenda (60-90 minutes):
1) Exec summary and business outcomes (10-15 min)
2) Usage & performance deep-dive (20-25 min)
3) Integration and roadmap alignment (15-20 min)
4) Risks, action items, and next steps (10-15 min)

Postmortems and follow-through:
- If an incident impacted SLA, a postmortem owner is assigned within 24 hours. Postmortems follow the company incident template and must include root cause, remediation, and preventative actions.
- Track action items in the CS backlog and review at weekly review meetings until closed.

Templates and examples (copyable):
- Customer kickoff agenda (bullet list)
- Integration test checklist (table row per test)
- Incident escalation email template:

Subject: [Sev1] <Customer> - <Short description>
To: support@redwood.ai; se-oncall@redwood.ai
CC: <Customer contacts>, csm-leads@redwood.ai
Body:
- Impact: <brief impact statement>
- First seen: <timestamp UTC>
- Request IDs: <list>
- Actions taken: <list>
- Immediate mitigation requested: <action>

Operational notes and tips:
- For Private deployments, include the onprem packaging version and kernel/torch build in every ticket to speed triage.
- When recommending quantization, always include a quality regression check using the customer's 50-100 sample prompt set.

Appendix (config snippets):
- Example batching config (YAML):
```
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 64
  max_latency_ms: 25
  dynamic_batching: true
```

- Example health-check query (PromQL):
```
sum(rate(redwood_request_errors_total[5m])) by (customer)
```
